definitions.explanation: Relating to the normal functions of a living organism. Used in scientific and medical contexts.
Describing a reaction that is automatic and beyond rational control — an instinctive like or dislike. Often used to express strong, involuntary aversion.

examples.japanese: {生理的|せいりてき}な⟦{反応|はんのう}→反応：04812_hannou⟧だ。
⟦{睡眠|すいみん}→睡眠：03359_suimin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧なものだ。
⟦{空腹|くうふく}→空腹：06532_kuufuku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{生理的|せいりてき}な⟦{欲求|よっきゅう}→欲求：13184_yokkyuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。
examples.english: Hunger is one of the physiological needs.

examples.japanese: {生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧だ。
examples.english: I just can't stand it — it's visceral.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{受|う}け{付|つ}けない→受け付ける：05683_uketsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I have a gut-level aversion to that person.

examples.japanese: ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧で、⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{鳥肌|とりはだ}→鳥肌：08544_torihada⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: I have an instinctive aversion to bugs — just seeing them gives me goosebumps.

notes: Sense 2 is very common in everyday Japanese. {生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧ (viscerally impossible/unbearable) and {生理的|せいりてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{受|う}け{付|つ}けない→受け付ける：05683_uketsukeru⟧ (can't tolerate on a gut level) are set phrases expressing strong involuntary aversion. This usage implies the reaction is beyond logic or reason — the speaker physically cannot tolerate something. Common collocations: {生理的|せいりてき}な⟦{欲求|よっきゅう}→欲求：13184_yokkyuu⟧ (physiological need), {生理的|せいりてき}{食塩水|しょくえんすい} (physiological saline).
